blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines, which has been classified as an upper-middle-income economy this year, spends less than one-third of 1 percent of its gross domestic product (GDP) on research and development, a data scientist said. Dr. Alicor Panao, an associate professor at the University of the Philippines, said in his analysis of data from the Unesco Institute for Statistics that the country spent only 0.276 percent of its GDP on research and development in 2020, the latest available figure in the dataset. The dataset compiles internationally comparable statistics on research spending and the research workforce through national submissions and contributions […]...
